questions.prompt: What appears in your folder after `git init`?
questions.explanation: git init creates the hidden .git folder that stores all version-control information.

questions.prompt: In the output of `git branch`, what does the asterisk `*` show?
options: The branch you are currently on
questions.explanation: The * marks the current branch.

questions.prompt: In `git push -u origin main`, what is `origin`?
options: The default name of the remote repository
questions.explanation: origin is the name given to the remote with `git remote add origin <url>`.

questions.prompt: Which file should go into `.gitignore`?
questions.explanation: .gitignore keeps secrets, dependencies and temporary files (.env, node_modules/, __pycache__/) out of Git.

questions.prompt: You committed on the wrong branch. Which command undoes that last commit (tutorial fix)?
questions.explanation: git reset HEAD~1 undoes the last commit (changes stay in your working dir); then switch branch and commit again.

questions.prompt: 'Available 24/7' and 'short response latency' are examples of…
questions.explanation: Functional = what the system should DO; non-functional = how it should BEHAVE (reliability, latency, scalability).

questions.prompt: N-layer vs N-tier: what does N-TIER describe?
questions.explanation: N-layer = logical separation (presentation, business, data access). N-tier = physical (client, server, database).

questions.prompt: In a layered architecture any layer may talk directly to any other layer.
questions.explanation: Each layer only communicates with the layer directly beneath it - clean separation of concerns.

questions.prompt: Plug-ins run in the SAME process as a minimal core. Which architecture?
questions.explanation: Microkernel: core + self-contained plug-ins in one application process (like a phone OS + apps).

questions.prompt: Producers publish events without knowing who reads them; consumers subscribe. Pattern?
questions.explanation: Event-bus: a central highway; producers broadcast, subscribers react asynchronously.

questions.prompt: Data streams through transforming steps connected by channels. Pattern?
questions.explanation: Filters transform the data; pipes pass it from one filter to the next.

questions.prompt: Like a stock market, buyers and sellers never interact directly. Pattern?
questions.explanation: A central broker coordinates communication and forwards requests to the right server.

questions.prompt: Decentralized network, every node is both client and server, no coordinator. Pattern?
questions.explanation: P2P: peers are equals, no central coordinator.

questions.prompt: In MVC, which part intercepts user input and updates the model and the view?
questions.explanation: Model = data & business logic, View = display, Controller = handles input.

questions.prompt: MySQL replication and Apache Hadoop are examples of which pattern?
questions.explanation: A master distributes work to identical slaves and aggregates results.

questions.prompt: No single algorithm solves it (AI); shared global memory + knowledge sources. Pattern?
questions.explanation: Blackboard = central memory, specialised knowledge sources, control component.

questions.prompt: Amazon: 'Order Placed' automatically triggers a confirmation email. Which style?
questions.explanation: An action produces an event that triggers reactions - event-driven architecture.

questions.prompt: Key difference between microkernel and microservices?
options: Plug-ins share one process; microservices run over a network
questions.explanation: Plug-ins run inside the same application process; microservices are distributed across servers.

questions.prompt: A typical DOWNSIDE of a layered (n-tier) architecture?
options: It can't be used for web apps
Extra latency from communication between layers
questions.explanation: Multiple layers can introduce latency due to communication between them.

questions.prompt: Interpreter architecture: what structure does the interpreter walk to execute code?
questions.explanation: The interpreter walks the abstract syntax tree representation of the language.

questions.prompt: Creating a pull request from the terminal: put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Branch → commit → push the branch → open the PR → merge after approval (then sync main with git pull).
questions.source: Week 3 Lecture 1 · 'Creating a Pull Request via Terminal'

questions.prompt: Create a new branch `feature/login` and switch to it, in one command.
questions.explanation: `git checkout -b` creates and switches in one step (`git switch -c` does the same in newer Git).
questions.source: Week 3 Lecture 1 · 'Creating a Pull Request via Terminal'

questions.prompt: Connect your local repo to the remote https://github.com/me/repo.git under the name origin.
questions.explanation: `git remote add <name> <url>`. Check it afterwards with `git remote -v`.
